assertionFindings.reason: Keep central Rāma worship focus: direct vande, bhaktiṃ prayaccha, bhajahu Rāma, trāhi trāhi and surrender support it. Hari in this context does not introduce a Krishna focus.

Keep central Hanumān narrative subject: Hanumān performs the crossing, search, fight, burning and return. The opening namāmi is also worship, but the projection conservatively omits that secondary role.
Keep supporting Sītā narrative subject: discovery, captivity, speech, grief, receiving the ring and giving the crest-jewel directly support it. Mother in dialogue refers to Sītā.
Keep central refuge: explicit sarana/saranāgata and Rāma vow dominate the Vibhīṣaṇa episode and earlier counsel to Rāvaṇa.
Keep supporting grace: kṛpā/anugraha are directly named and causally credited for success, strength and encounters with saints.
Keep supporting service: Rāma kāju, sevaka and dāsa explicitly motivate Hanumān action; not merely inferred from heroic activity.
Keep supporting longing: Sītā viraha and Rāma viyoga are named and sustained through fire, water, breath and bodily images.

Keep supporting name-power:239 explicitly says chanting his name severs worldly bonds;350 makes the name a guard,454 dispeller of threefold suffering. Ring157 alone would be weaker but is not sole support.
Keep supporting praise: opening invocations praise Rāma and Hanumān;161 recounts Rāma virtues;388 and407 enact victory acclamations and song.
Keep supporting remembrance: repeated sumiri/sambhāri/sumirana, hṛdaya and dhyāna evidence is explicit and correctly attributed.
Keep supporting ethical conduct: nīti, protection of envoys, truthful counsel, restraint regarding another wife, and rejection of lust/anger/pride/greed extend beyond generic devotional vocabulary.
